thread.title: Pennsylvania is a frontrunner for new Apple campus, says Bloomberg

author: Urvaksh Karkaria
title: Pennsylvania is a frontrunner for new Apple campus, says Bloomberg
text: Mar 8, 2018, 3:50pm EST Updated Mar 8, 2018, 3:58pm EST Pittsburgh is among the 20 cities still in the running for Amazon's second headquarters, but a new analysis indicates Pennsylvania may have a better shot at landing Apple's new U.S. campus. Apple Inc . (Nasdaq: AAPL), in January announced plans for a new U.S. campus as part of a broader plan to create 20,000 jobs in the U.S. The new campus, part of a planned $30 billion in capital expenditure over the next five years, will initially house customer tech support employees. The Washington Post ranked Pittsburgh towards the bottom of its list of Amazon finalists with better tech economies. Unlike e-commerce giant Amazon, the iPhone maker is not taking a bidding war approach to its site search – giving some room to speculate. Apple has said it already narrowed its focus, and even confirmed it ruled out Texas for its next corporate campus. While Pittsburgh hasn't been specifically floated by Apple, a new report from Bloomberg indicates Pennsylvania is a potential frontrunner. Based on factors, such as human capital, tax incentives, transportation, existing Apple offices and data center, the company “seems likely to choose among northeastern states such as Pennsylvania, Massachusetts and upstate New York; North Carolina and Florida in the southeast; and Midwestern states like Illinois and Wisconsin,” Bloomberg noted in a joint analysis with Moody Analytics. Both Philadelphia and Pittsburgh surfaced on some of the metrics Bloomberg considered. Philadelphia was among the cities ranked for human capital and transportation, while Pittsburgh nabbed a spot in both those categories, as well as the smaller corporate office metric. Pennsylvania also has 253 suppliers, which can provide Apple with many of the key components needed to build their products. It's also worth nothing that Carlisle, Pa. has an Apple Care Repair Center. The Bloomberg assessment puts Pennsylvania as one of the top options for Apple, according to Moody’s Analytics. ( See the above slideshow for a statewide rundown ) “The cities were chosen because they emphasize bachelor’s degrees instead of advanced engineering degrees, which arguably fit better with Apple’s plans to recruit technical support people, rather than those working on products and operations.” It’s not clear how much technical talent Apple will need, so the company may not put as much focus on human capital, said Moody’s Senior Economist Adam Ozimek . Given that the new campus will be a customer support center, Apple will focus on cities that have a propensity for growth in the workforce and in-migration trends, site selection consultant John Boyd Jr. said. "Tech support centers — even for deep pocketed, "employers of choice" like Apple — do have higher rates of turnover," Boyd said. Apple is expected to make a site selection decision on the new campus later this year. The East Coast has an advantage — the ability to provide customer support before existing call centers in Texas and California open for the day, as well as its proximity to hundreds of suppliers, Bloomberg noted. Apple could also consider the northwest, where it has a couple of offices, including an R&D center for cloud services in Seattle, and several suppliers.
